bug_semantics: Apache OpenMeetings wired the remember-me authentication strategy to a repository-shipped default encryption key, and later also shipped a fixed salt, so deployments that retained the defaults shared the cryptographic material protecting cookies whose plaintext contains username, password, login type, and domain ID. A thief of such a cookie could use the public defaults to recover the stored credentials; the material was not automatically rotated.
flaw_origin: Commit ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f first added remember.me.encryption.key=27574200-a56f-410a-b2c9-3aa3b4b9389a to openmeetings.properties, injected it into Application, and passed it to OmAuthenticationStrategy for remember-me cookie cryptography. Its direct parent contains none of those key/configuration/constructor lines. Follow-up 409f74a85cadd20351d0c8e333d116446db27a12 added the fixed salt abrakadabra but did not create the already-existing hard-coded-key flaw.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Maxim Solodovnik <solomax666@gmail.com> as both author and committer, its message is only '[OPENMEETINGS-2593] wicket and friends', and git interpret-trailers --parse returns no trailers or AI marker
evidence: Apache's CVE-2026-33266 CNA record is PUBLISHED and specifies Apache OpenMeetings >=6.1.0 and <9.0.0 as affected, with 9.0.0 as the boundary; the Apache oss-security notice says the default remember-me key was not auto-rotated and exposed full user credentials from a stolen cookie, and tracks OPENMEETINGS-2813.

git log -L 23,23:openmeetings-web/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/classes/openmeetings.properties 6.1.0 resolves the hard-coded key line to ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f, a single-parent commit with parent 86351d4e34504f14d88af191bd924a33c0ea073a.

git show ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f shows openmeetings.properties:21-23 adding the public default key, Application.java:194-200 injecting it and constructing OmAuthenticationStrategy(encryptionKey), and OmAuthenticationStrategy.java:30-31,71-76 using that key for the LoggedIn cookie crypt implementation.

Direct parent-tree verification with git show/git grep on 86351d4e34504f14d88af191bd924a33c0ea073a shows the properties file has only scrypt.cost before the timeout section and has no remember.me.encryption.key, fixed UUID, or OmAuthenticationStrategy(String encryptionKey) mechanism.

Commit 409f74a85cadd20351d0c8e333d116446db27a12 subsequently added remember.me.encryption.salt=abrakadabra and passed it into the same strategy; this strengthened the public-default mechanism but postdates the BIC that already hard-coded and consumed the encryption key.

git show c407437744ec5ae3c4ae675ac0ce48dbf24f1fed and its parent prove the direct fix: parent fff5e2a769759fa456eab2a14c4b50671d792486 still contains the fixed key and salt, while the fix removes both defaults, adds remember.me.rotation.days=30, stores a generated key in Configuration, rotates it when missing/short/expired, and switches cookie crypto to the stored key.

Tag ancestry checks show ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f is not an ancestor of 6.0.0 but is an ancestor of tag 6.1.0 (c03148c5a5c759af1641eacf8584e3cf951774de); c407437744ec5ae3c4ae675ac0ce48dbf24f1fed is not an ancestor of 8.1.0 but is an ancestor of 9.0.0 (bff7dfecd5044418471ffc3733f235226585ea06).
git cat-file -p ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f verifies identical human author/committer identities and no commit-message trailers; no commit-object AI authorship signal exists on the BIC.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and the vendor/CNA release boundaries agree with the source history. The smallest public object that first creates the flawed lifecycle is ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f: in one single-parent commit it ships a fixed encryption key, injects that value at application startup, and uses it for remember-me cookies containing credentials. Line history points to that commit and the immediate parent tree lacks the mechanism, so this is not a move, revert, release carrier, or fix. The next-day fixed-salt commit is a later aggravating change, not the first writer of the hard-coded-key mechanism. Commit c407437744ec5ae3c4ae675ac0ce48dbf24f1fed directly removes the fixed key and salt and adds generated, persisted, periodically rotated key material; ancestry places the BIC after 6.0.0 and by 6.1.0, and places the fix after 8.1.0 and in 9.0.0. Finally, attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI/bot/co-author/generated trailer. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
